triplets.head: International law in cyberspace
triplets.tail: Broad international consensus that existing international law applies to state conduct in cyberspace

triplets.head: UN Charter
triplets.tail: Applies in its entirety to state activities in cyberspace

triplets.head: Prohibition on the use of force (Art. 2(4) UN Charter)
triplets.tail: Applies to cyber operations whose scale and effects are comparable to conventional armed attacks

triplets.head: Right of self-defence (Art. 51 UN Charter)
triplets.tail: Applies if a cyber operation amounts to an armed attack

triplets.head: Principle of non-intervention
triplets.tail: States may not use cyber means to coercively interfere in the domaine réservé of other states

triplets.head: International humanitarian law (IHL)
triplets.tail: Applies to cyber operations conducted in the context of armed conflict

triplets.head: International human rights law (IHRL)
triplets.tail: Human rights obligations apply online as they do offline

triplets.head: Law of State Responsibility
triplets.tail: States bear legal responsibility for internationally wrongful cyber acts attributable to them

triplets.head: Due diligence obligation
triplets.tail: A state must not knowingly allow its territory to be used for cyber operations harmful to other states' rights

triplets.head: Peaceful settlement of disputes (Art. 2(3) UN Charter)
triplets.tail: States must seek peaceful resolution of cyber-related disputes

triplets.head: UN GGE 2013 report
triplets.tail: First to affirm that international law and the UN Charter apply in cyberspace

triplets.head: UN GGE 2015 report
triplets.tail: Adopted 11 voluntary non-binding norms of responsible state behaviour

triplets.head: 11 UN cyber norms
triplets.tail: UNGA Resolution 70/237 (2015)

triplets.head: UN Norm 1
triplets.tail: States should cooperate to increase stability and security in ICT use and prevent harmful practices

triplets.head: UN Norm 2
triplets.tail: States should consider all relevant information in ICT incidents including attribution challenges

triplets.head: UN Norm 3
triplets.tail: States should not knowingly allow their territory to be used for internationally wrongful cyber acts

triplets.head: UN Norm 4
triplets.tail: States should cooperate to combat terrorist and criminal misuse of ICTs

triplets.head: UN Norm 5
triplets.tail: States should respect human rights online including privacy and freedom of expression

triplets.head: UN Norm 6
triplets.tail: States should not conduct or support ICT activity that damages critical infrastructure

triplets.head: UN Norm 7
triplets.tail: States should protect critical infrastructure from ICT threats

triplets.head: UN Norm 8
triplets.tail: States should respond to requests for assistance when another state's critical infrastructure is attacked

triplets.head: UN Norm 9
triplets.tail: States should ensure supply chain integrity and prevent proliferation of malicious ICT tools

triplets.head: UN Norm 10
triplets.tail: States should encourage responsible vulnerability disclosure and share remedies

triplets.head: UN Norm 11
triplets.tail: States should not harm or misuse emergency response teams (CERTs/CSIRTs)
